tourist_spots.exact_location_address: San Carlos - Basista - Bayambang Road, Barangay Bani, Bayambang, 2423 Pangasinan (Google Maps Place IDs: ChIJhRf7wT5JkTMRwcDsipUyS0o / ChIJg1QXwiJJkTMRsD4M75HaAu0; Coordinates: 15°49′11″N 120°26′39″E)
tourist_spots.detailed_description: Inaugurated on April 5, 2019 to commemorate Bayambang's 405th Founding Anniversary, the 400th year of the St. Vincent Ferrer Parish, and the 600th death anniversary of St. Vincent Ferrer, this 50.23-meter (164.8-foot) monument holds the Guinness World Record for the Tallest Bamboo Sculpture in the world. Privately funded by the Kasama Kita sa Barangay Foundation and designed by JQS Builders using 3D polygon technology (~5,000 polygons), its interior frame uses 600 tons of structural steel clad with 60 tons (22,626 panels) of treated engineered bamboo imported from China, anchored on a 7.5-meter-deep concrete foundation to withstand typhoons and earthquakes. The surrounding park features an air-conditioned hilltop chapel, meditation gardens, the Jesus Way to Resurrection / Stations of the Cross statues, spacious parking, and a food park.

tourist_spots.official_name: Archdiocesan Shrine and Parish of St. Vincent Ferrer (Bayambang Church)
tourist_spots.exact_location_address: RF54+F9V, Roxas Street, Town Proper (Poblacion), Bayambang, 2423 Pangasinan (Google Maps Place ID: ChIJ____DxlJkTMR8hfnKrKiJ10; Phone: +63 75 529 2024)
tourist_spots.detailed_description: Established by Dominican missionaries in 1619 (with its current brick structure dating back to 1869), the St. Vincent Ferrer Parish Church has stood for more than 400 years at the center of Bayambang opposite the historic Municipal Plaza. Featuring High Renaissance, Baroque, and Neo-Gothic architectural details with thick brick walls, cavernous acoustics, stained-glass windows, and a long wedding aisle, it enshrines the first-class holy relic of St. Vincent Ferrer at the foot of his statue on the main retablo. In April 2025, Archbishop Socrates Villegas elevated the church to an Archdiocesan Shrine.

tourist_spots.official_name: Sky Plaza & Ayat ni Apo Hesus Shrine (Christ the Redeemer Statue & Marian Grotto)
tourist_spots.exact_location_address: 3R5G+6WR & 3R6H+2QP, Barangay Batchelor East, Natividad, 2446 Pangasinan (Google Maps Place IDs: ChIJqzGbfiIckTMRghTJE07iInY / ChIJxzva5csdkTMRX9ui9b5s5-Y)
tourist_spots.detailed_description: Perched atop a hill at the foot of the Caraballo Mountains in Barangay Batchelor East, Sky Plaza is Natividad's premier pilgrimage and eco-tourism destination. Visitors pass through the 'Arch of Love' and ascend a concrete stairway (287 steps to the first viewing station/Holy Cross, and up to 1,217 total steps to the summit) featuring a Virgin Mary (Lourdes) Grotto, a 30-foot Holy Cross, an octagon-shaped multipurpose hall, a hilltop chapel, picnic tables, a seasonal 120-meter zipline, and the crowning 40-foot white concrete-and-fiberglass statue of Christ the Redeemer known locally in Ilocano as 'Ayat ni Apo Hesus' ('God's Love'), completed in 2014. (Note: While sometimes informally referred to as 'Our Lady of Caysasay Shrine'—which is in Taal, Batangas—Natividad's hilltop shrine at Sky Plaza features the Ayat ni Apo Hesus Shrine and Virgin Mary Grotto, while the town parish is Our Lady's Nativity Parish Church).

entrance_and_venue_fees.parking_fee: PHP 20.00 - PHP 50.00 depending on vehicle size

tourist_spots.official_name: Maranum Falls (Batchelor East, Natividad)
tourist_spots.exact_location_address: Barangay Batchelor East, Natividad, 2446 Pangasinan (Google Maps Place ID: ChIJZSf_0DcckTMR1vE3tZjLkFw; Phone: +63 965 119 4216)
tourist_spots.detailed_description: Located in the Caraballo foothills of Barangay Batchelor East beyond Sky Plaza, Maranum Falls takes its name from the Pangasinan/Ilocano word 'maranum' meaning 'many waters,' as its powerful cascade never dries up even during the summer dry season. Surrounded by lush mountain forest and giant boulders feeding into the Viray River, it features a wide natural catch basin with crystal-clear, cold mountain water and safety handrails along the 10-to-45-minute forest trail. By municipal ordinance, food and liquor are strictly prohibited inside the waterfall area (water and non-alcoholic drinks are permitted).

tourist_spots.official_name: Minor Basilica of Saint Dominic (St. Dominic de Guzman Parish Church)
tourist_spots.exact_location_address: Malong Street, Poblacion, San Carlos City, 2420 Pangasinan (Google Maps Place ID: ChIJ-1bledJEkTMRITopbE7uFu0; Coordinates: 15°55′35″N 120°20′50″E; Phone: +63 75 523 2218)
tourist_spots.detailed_description: Founded by Dominican missionaries in 1587 in what was then Binalatongan, this is the oldest parish in Pangasinan. The current massive Baroque red-brick (ladrillo) structure was built between 1770 and 1773 under Fr. Cristobal Ausina and reinforced after the earthquakes of 1789, 1796, and 1799. Measuring 89 yards (81 meters) long, 22 yards (20 meters) wide, and 16.5 meters high with upper and lower stained-glass windows, it was once the largest Catholic church in the Philippines in the late 18th century. Its belfry once held a 3,990-kg (4-ton) bell cast in 1815. On July 26, 2022, Pope Francis bestowed the title of Minor Basilica upon the church, solemnly proclaimed on January 14, 2023—making it the first and only Minor Basilica of St. Dominic in Asia.

Admire the 250+-year-old Baroque brick facade, terracotta reliefs, and two-tiered stained-glass interior

tourist_spots.detailed_description: Located directly between Tayug/Natividad and Umingan along the Eastern Pangasinan mountain corridor, San Quintin offers two highly rated nature and water escapes: Dipalo River Park (a clean, cold mountain river park with three terraced waterfall-like cascades and riverside cottages) and Ramirez Picnic Garden Resort (an eco-friendly family resort with a wave pool, adult and kiddie swimming pools, a fishing pond, basketball/volleyball courts, and videoke).
